QF.id: VII Introduction to Securities Broking Operations_42

question.text: In an Offer for Sale (OFS) through stock exchanges, if an investor defaults in pay-in, what penalty is charged?

explanation.text: The Logic: In case of default in pay-in by any investor in OFS, 10% of the order value is charged as penalty. The same penalty is repeated in the IPF contribution list, and the Settlement Guarantee Fund is not available for OFS. The Trap: Institutional investors may place orders without upfront margin, but those orders cannot be cancelled/modified except for upward revision; non-institutional investors must pay 100% upfront margin. Note: The 10% penalty applies specifically to investor pay-in default in OFS.
